title: ICMR Antimicrobial Stewardship Treatment Guidelines for Common Syndromes

chunks.topic: Judicious Antibiotic Use in Upper Respiratory Infections
chunks.content: Over 85% to 90% of acute upper respiratory tract infections, uncomplicated bronchitis, and sore throat cases in outpatient primary care are etiology-confirmed viral illnesses. Empirical antibiotic therapy (such as Azithromycin, Amoxicillin-Clavulanate, or Cefixime) is strongly discouraged for uncomplicated viral coryza, watery rhinorrhea, and mild sore throats as it provides no clinical acceleration of recovery and accelerates the emergence of multidrug-resistant pathogens across community reservoirs. Symptomatic management with warm saline gargles, honey-ginger demulcent, hydration, and steam inhalation constitutes appropriate standard care.
chunks.contraindications: Do not take leftover, non-prescribed, or shared antibiotics from previous illnesses or family members.
chunks.warnings: Antibiotics require a verified physical medical prescription and must be taken for the complete course if prescribed by a registered physician. Seek clinician evaluation if high fever persists >3 days, thick purulent sputum with severe pleuritic chest pain develops, or breathing becomes labored.
chunks.home_care: Warm water hydration, steam inhalation for nasal congestion relief, warm saline throat gargles twice daily, and adequate sleep.
chunks.citation: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (2nd Edition, 2024), Respiratory Tract Infections Section, pp. 31-39.
